baseline.note: Library citations read at the pinned commit: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165 (WittVector.fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R for p-adically complete R with p not a unit), Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634 (PreTilt), Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52 (WittVector). Neither library defines perfectoid rings, the cotangent complex, THH, cyclotomic spectra, A_crys of a semiperfect ring, de Rham–Witt complexes or the Nygaard filtration (declaration index searched for Perfectoid, Cotangent, TopologicalHochschild, Cyclotomic, DeRhamWitt, Nygaard, Syntomic).

summary: Bhatt, Morrow and Scholze construct 'motivic' filtrations on THH, TC^-, TP and TC of quasisyntomic rings by quasisyntomic descent of the double-speed Postnikov filtration from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings, where these spectra are even (Theorem 1.12). The graded pieces are the Nygaard-completed prismatic complex Δ̂_A = π_0TC^- unfolded, its Nygaard filtration and Breuil–Kisin twists, and the syntomic complexes Z_p(n) = fib(φ − can). Δ̂ recovers A_inf-cohomology AΩ for smooth O_C-algebras (Theorem 1.8) and crystalline cohomology in characteristic p via Nygaard-completed A_crys (Theorems 1.10, 8.17); the Nygaard filtration matches the Lη filtration. Z_p(n) is logarithmic de Rham–Witt cohomology in characteristic p and truncated p-adic nearby cycles over O_C (Theorem 1.15). HC^- and HP are filtered by derived de Rham cohomology (Theorem 1.17), and relative THH over S[z] with a Frobenius descent gives Breuil–Kisin cohomology of proper smooth formal O_K-schemes (Theorem 1.2). The atlas already plans this material: RefinedTraceMethods RT.6 owns BMS2's THH/TC^-/TP computation and the motivic filtration, PrismaticCohomology PR.3–PR.4 the Nygaard filtration, syntomic twists and the nearby-cycle and log de Rham–Witt comparisons, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 the quasisyntomic site, and AInfCohomology AI.7 Breuil–Kisin cohomology. So BMS2 becomes a source of those layers, with its supporting constructions routed to them; one input (Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's K ≃ τ_{≥0}TC) goes to the henselian-pairs Part II proposed by that extraction. No new roadmap is needed. Twelve misprints are recorded (eleven persist in the published version); no error or gap was found.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Let K be a discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field k, ϖ ∈ O_K a uniformizer, 𝔖 = W(k)[[z]] with the surjection θ̃ : 𝔖 → O_K, z ↦ ϖ, whose kernel is generated by an Eisenstein polynomial E(z), and φ the Frobenius of W(k) with z ↦ z^p. A Breuil–Kisin module is a finitely generated 𝔖-module M with an isomorphism M ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔖[1/E] ≅ M[1/E].
items.note: R07.4 constructs the power-series coefficient ring and Frobenius modules with the Eisenstein height bound; AI.7 uses them as the values of cohomology. BMS2's definition allows torsion and requires no height bound.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: Breuil–Kisin cohomology of proper smooth formal O_K-schemes
items.statement: For a proper smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over O_K there is an 𝔖-linear cohomology theory RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) with a φ-linear Frobenius such that (1) RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf ≃ RΓ_{A_inf}(𝔛_{O_C}); in particular RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) is a perfect 𝔖-complex, φ induces RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔖[1/E] ≃ RΓ_𝔖(𝔛)[1/E], every H^i_𝔖(𝔛) is a Breuil–Kisin module, and after scalar extension to A_inf[1/μ] one recovers étale cohomology; (2) RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) ⊗^L_{𝔖,θ} O_K ≃ RΓ_dR(𝔛/O_K) for θ = θ̃ ∘ φ; (3) RΓ_𝔖(𝔛) ⊗^L_𝔖 W(k) ≃ RΓ_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) along the map that is Frobenius on W(k) and z ↦ 0. Here 𝔖 ⊂ A_inf by Frobenius on W(k) and z ↦ [ϖ^♭]^p.
items.note: AI.7 constructs the 𝔖-valued cohomology and compares it with BMS2 §11's trace construction; Bhatt–Scholze reprove it with the prismatic site (Remark 1.3).

items.name: Frobenius twists force de Rham torsion to have length divisible by p
items.statement: For K = Q_p(p^{1/p}), θ : 𝔖 → O_K sends z to p, so RΓ_dR(𝔛/O_K) is the base change of a complex over Z_p; hence the length of each H^i_dR(𝔛/O_K)_tors, and of each indecomposable summand, is a multiple of p.

items.name: Theorem 1.6: TC^- of perfectoid rings is A_inf
items.statement: For a perfectoid ring R there is a canonical φ-equivariant isomorphism π_0 TC^-(R; Z_p) ≅ A_inf(R), and π_*TC^-(R; Z_p), π_*TP(R; Z_p) and π_*THH(R; Z_p) are identified explicitly with the maps between them (Hesselholt for R = O_{C_p}).
items.note: RT.6 owns BMS2's computation of THH, TC^- and TP; AI.0 owns A_inf and θ.

items.name: The quasisyntomic site
items.statement: A ring A is quasisyntomic if it is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{A/Z_p} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]. For p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion, A → B is quasisyntomic (resp. quasismooth; resp. a cover) if B is p-completely flat (resp. faithfully flat) over A and L_{B/A} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0] (resp. is p-completely flat). QSyn is the category of quasisyntomic rings, qSyn_A the quasisyntomic A-algebras; both are sites for quasisyntomic covers, with pushouts the p-completed tensor products, and RΓ_syn(A, F) is cohomology of the sheafification. p-adic completions of smooth algebras over perfectoid rings and p-complete Noetherian lci rings are quasisyntomic.
items.locator: Definition 1.7, p. 204; Definition 4.10, Example 4.12 and Lemmas 4.15–4.17, pp. 223–225
items.note: DD.0 defines quasisyntomic maps and proves 'the compatibility with the alternative formulations in BMS2 §4'; DD.5 constructs the site. The quasismooth notion is used only for the p-complete HKR theorem.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: AΩ from topological Hochschild homology
items.statement: Let A be the p-adic completion of a smooth O_C-algebra. There is a functorial φ-equivariant isomorphism of E_∞-A_inf-algebras AΩ_A ≃ RΓ_syn(A, π_0TC^-(−; Z_p)) = Δ̂_A; on the basis of quasiregular semiperfectoids the presheaf π_0TC^- is already a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology.
items.locator: Theorem 1.8 and Remark 1.9, p. 204; Theorem 9.6, p. 286
items.note: RT.6 constructs the trace-to-prismatic comparison and PR.6 proves AΩ_R ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf}; together they give the statement. BMS2's own proof (almost mathematics, Lη and left Kan extension to proj-quasisyntomic objects) is routed to RT.6 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.10: crystalline cohomology from topological Hochschild homology
items.statement: For k perfect of characteristic p and A a smooth k-algebra there is a functorial φ-equivariant isomorphism of E_∞-W(k)-algebras RΓ_crys(A/W(k)) ≃ RΓ_syn(A, π_0TC^-(−; Z_p)), obtained by identifying π_0TC^- with the Nygaard completion of the sheaf A_crys (compare Fontaine–Messing).
items.locator: Theorem 1.10, p. 205; Theorem 8.17 and the following paragraph, p. 276
items.note: Planned in RT.6's trace-to-prismatic comparison, since Bhatt–Scholze identify prismatic cohomology of a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra with A_crys.

items.name: The Nygaard-completed prismatic complex Δ̂_A and its Nygaard filtration
items.statement: For a quasisyntomic ring A, Δ̂_A = RΓ_syn(A, π_0TC^-(−; Z_p)) = gr^0TC^-(A; Z_p) = gr^0TP(A; Z_p) is an E_∞-Z_p-algebra with the complete Nygaard filtration 𝒩^{≥•}Δ̂_A obtained from the abutment filtration of the homotopy fixed point spectral sequence; it is an E_∞-algebra in the completed filtered derived category, with Frobenius φ. (Bhatt–Scholze identify it with the Nygaard completion of prismatic cohomology.)
items.locator: Remark 1.11, p. 205; Theorem 1.12(3), p. 206; Construction 7.7, p. 257

items.name: Theorem 1.12(1)–(2): evenness and the motivic filtrations on THH, TC^- and TP
items.statement: Let A be quasisyntomic. Locally on qSyn_A the spectra THH(−; Z_p), TC^-(−; Z_p) and TP(−; Z_p) are concentrated in even degrees, and Fil^n THH(A; Z_p) = RΓ_syn(A, τ_{≥2n}THH(−; Z_p)), and likewise for TC^- and TP, are complete exhaustive decreasing multiplicative Z-indexed filtrations.
items.note: The existence of the filtration was conjectured by Hesselholt. RT.6 owns 'the BMS2 quasisyntomic THH/TC^-/TP computation and motivic-filtration interface'.

items.name: Theorem 1.12(3): Breuil–Kisin twists of Δ̂_A
items.statement: Δ̂_A{1} = gr^1TP(A; Z_p)[−2] with its Nygaard filtration is an invertible module over the filtered ring Δ̂_A in the completed filtered derived category (not necessarily invertible over the unfiltered ring); Δ̂_A{1}/𝒩^{≥n} is invertible over Δ̂_A/𝒩^{≥n}; if A admits a map from a perfectoid ring then Δ̂_A{1} ≅ Δ̂_A; and Δ̂_A{1} ⊗_{Δ̂_A} A ≅ A canonically. M{i} = M ⊗ Δ̂_A{1}^{⊗i}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.12(3), p. 206; proof of Theorem 1.12 with Lemma 7.14, pp. 260–261

items.name: Theorem 1.12(4): graded pieces of the motivic filtrations
items.statement: gr^nTHH(A; Z_p) ≃ 𝒩^nΔ̂_A{n}[2n] ≃ 𝒩^nΔ̂_A[2n], gr^nTC^-(A; Z_p) ≃ 𝒩^{≥n}Δ̂_A{n}[2n] and gr^nTP(A; Z_p) ≃ Δ̂_A{n}[2n], with multiplicative spectral sequences E_2^{ij} = H^{i−j}(𝒩^{−j}Δ̂_A) ⇒ π_{−i−j}THH(A; Z_p) and similarly for TC^- and TP.

items.name: Theorem 1.12(5): the motivic filtration on TC and the syntomic complexes Z_p(n)
items.statement: φ : TC^- → TP preserves the filtrations, so Fil^nTC(A; Z_p) = hofib(φ − can : Fil^nTC^- → Fil^nTP) filters TC(A; Z_p) = hofib(φ − can : TC^- → TP), with gr^n TC(A; Z_p)[−2n] = Z_p(n)(A) = hofib(φ − can : 𝒩^{≥n}Δ̂_A{n} → Δ̂_A{n}) and a spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^{i−j}(Z_p(−j)(A)) ⇒ π_{−i−j}TC(A; Z_p). Over a perfectoid base, trivializing the twist, φ on 𝒩^{≥n}Δ̂_A{n} is the divided Frobenius ξ̃^{−n}φ.

items.name: Theorem 1.15(1): syntomic complexes of smooth algebras in characteristic p
items.statement: For A smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p and X = Spec A there is an isomorphism of sheaves of complexes on the pro-étale site of X: Rλ_*Z_p(n) ≃ WΩ^n_{X,log}[−n], where λ : qSyn_A^op → X_proét.
items.locator: Theorem 1.15(1), p. 208; Corollary 8.21 and Remark 8.22, p. 282
items.note: PR.4 proves 'the stated truncation and nearby-cycle/logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons under BS22/BMS2's hypotheses'. Related to Hesselholt and Geisser–Hesselholt; an analogue of Milne's conjecture with the quasisyntomic topology.

items.name: Theorem 1.15(2): syntomic complexes as truncated p-adic nearby cycles
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C with generic fibre X and ψ : X_ét → 𝔛_ét. Then Z/p^n(i) ≃ τ^{≤i}Rψ_*Z/p^n(i) on 𝔛_ét, compatibly in n (so Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i}Rψ_*Z_p(i) on the pro-étale site); in particular the nearby cycle sheaves R^iψ_*Z/p^n are flat over Z/p^n.
items.locator: Theorem 1.15(2), p. 208; Theorem 10.1 and Remarks 10.2–10.3, p. 293

items.name: Theorem 1.17: negative and periodic cyclic homology via derived de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For R ∈ QSyn and A ∈ qSyn_R, Fil^nHC^-(A/R; Z_p) = RΓ_syn(A, τ_{≥2n}HC^-(−/R; Z_p)) and Fil^nHP(A/R; Z_p) are complete exhaustive multiplicative filtrations with gr^nHC^- ≃ L̂Ω^{≥n}_{A/R}[2n] and gr^nHP ≃ L̂Ω_{A/R}[2n] (p-adically and Hodge completed derived de Rham), with the corresponding multiplicative spectral sequences.
items.note: DD.5 notes that 'RefinedTraceMethods RT.1/6 uses these objects in HKR/negative-cyclic filtrations'. Antieau removed the p-completion.

items.name: Non-abelian derived functors as left Kan extensions
items.statement: sCAlg_R = 𝒫_Σ(CAlg_R^poly), and any functor from finitely generated polynomial R-algebras to an ∞-category with sifted colimits extends uniquely to a sifted-colimit-preserving functor on simplicial commutative R-algebras (preserving all colimits if the original preserves finite coproducts) ([HTT, 5.5.8–5.5.9]).

items.name: The cotangent complex, its exterior powers and the transitivity filtration
items.statement: L_{A/R} = Ω^1_{P•/R} ⊗_{P•} A for a simplicial polynomial resolution, equivalently the left Kan extension of Ω^1 (and ∧^jL of Ω^j); ∧^iL_{A/R} ≃ Ω^i_{A/R} for A smooth; for A → B → C the transitivity triangle and the length-i filtration of ∧^iL_{C/A} with graded pieces (∧^jL_{B/A} ⊗^L_B C) ⊗^L_C ∧^{i−j}L_{C/B}.

items.name: Derived Hochschild homology, HC^- and HP
items.statement: HH(A/R) is the diagonal of C•(P•/R) for a flat simplicial resolution (Shukla homology), equivalently the left Kan extension of the usual Hochschild complex from polynomial algebras; it carries a circle action, and HC^-(A/R) = HH(A/R)^{hT}, HP(A/R) = HH(A/R)^{tT}, with the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences.
items.note: RT.1 constructs Hochschild chains 'including derived tensor products where flatness is absent' and the cyclic variants.

items.name: Universal property of HH(A/R)
items.statement: HH(A/R) is the initial T-equivariant E_∞-R-algebra with a non-equivariant map from A: HH(A/R) ≃ A ⊗_{E_∞-R} T, computed on polynomial algebras as A ⊗^L_{A⊗_RA} A.

items.name: The HKR theorem and the HKR filtration
items.statement: For A smooth over R the antisymmetrization Ω^n_{A/R} → HH_n(A/R) is an isomorphism; by left Kan extension HH(−/R) on sCAlg_R has a T-equivariant complete descending N-indexed filtration Fil_HKR with gr^i ≃ ∧^iL_{−/R}[i] (trivial T-action), a weak Postnikov tower.
items.note: RT.1 plans the smooth characteristic-zero HKR comparison only.

items.name: THH, the cyclotomic Frobenius, TC^-, TP and TC
items.statement: For an E_∞-ring A, THH(A) is the initial T-equivariant E_∞-ring with a non-equivariant map from A; the Tate diagonal gives the T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant Frobenius φ_p : THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p}; TC^-(A) = THH(A)^{hT}, TP(A) = THH(A)^{tT}, with can : TC^- → TP and, for connective A, φ = φ_p^{hT} : TC^-(A; Z_p) → TP(A; Z_p), and TC(A; Z_p) = hofib(φ − can) ([NS18]); p-completions commute with (−)^{hT} and, for bounded below spectra, with (−)_{hT} and (−)^{tT}.

items.name: TP as homotopy fixed points of the Tate construction
items.statement: For connective A, TP(A; Z_p) ≃ (THH(A)^{tC_p})^{hT} ([NS18, Lemma II.4.2]), which gives φ^{hT} : TC^-(A; Z_p) → TP(A; Z_p); moreover π_0TC^-(A; Z_p) ≅ π_0TP(A; Z_p) via can.

items.name: Bökstedt periodicity
items.statement: π_*THH(F_p) = F_p[u] with u ∈ π_2 ([Bök85], [NS18, Thm. IV.4.4]); this is the only non-formal input on THH that BMS2 uses.
items.locator: §2.3, p. 216; Remark 1.5, p. 203; proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 244
items.note: L.5 proves 'the calculation of THH/TR/TC for perfect fields'.

items.name: THH relative to THH(Z) is Hochschild homology
items.statement: For a commutative ring A there is a natural T-equivariant equivalence of E_∞-rings THH(A) ⊗_{THH(Z)} Z ≃ HH(A), also after p-completion; π_iTHH(Z) is finite for i > 0 (Z/j for i = 2j − 1, 0 for other i > 0, by Bökstedt).

items.name: Flat descent for exterior powers of the cotangent complex (Bhatt)
items.statement: For a base ring R and i ≥ 0, A ↦ ∧^i_A L_{A/R} is an fpqc sheaf with values in D(R); for p-completely faithfully flat maps of derived p-complete R-algebras with bounded p^∞-torsion the p-completions satisfy descent. (Whether hyperdescent holds is left open.)
items.locator: Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.2, pp. 217–218; Remark 4.9, p. 223
items.note: DD.5: 'Prove descent for completed cotangent exterior powers, derived de Rham and its specified filtration/completion.'

items.name: Weak Postnikov towers and right t-exact functors
items.statement: If {M_n} is a weak Postnikov tower of connective modules over a connective E_1-ring S with limit M, and F : D(S) → Sp is right t-exact, then {F(M_n)} is a weak Postnikov tower with limit F(M).

items.name: Flat descent for Hochschild and topological Hochschild homology
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, HH(−/R), HC^-(−/R), HH(−/R)_{hT} and HP(−/R) are fpqc sheaves on R-algebras, and THH, TC^-, THH_{hT} and TP are fpqc sheaves on commutative rings; the same holds for (−)_{hC_n}, (−)^{tC_n} and all TR^n.

items.name: p-complete Tor amplitude and p-complete flatness
items.statement: M ∈ D(A) has p-complete Tor amplitude in [a, b] (resp. is p-completely (faithfully) flat) if M ⊗^L_A A/p has Tor amplitude in [a, b] (resp. is a (faithfully) flat A/p-module in degree 0); A/p may be replaced by A/p^n; the notion is insensitive to derived p-completion, stable under base change and descends along p-completely faithfully flat maps.

items.name: p-completely flat complexes over rings with bounded p^∞-torsion
items.statement: If A has bounded p^∞-torsion and M ∈ D(A) is derived p-complete with p-complete Tor amplitude in [a, b], then M ∈ D^{[a,b]}(A); a p-completely flat M is a classically p-complete module with bounded p^∞-torsion, M/p^n flat over A/p^n and M ⊗ A[p^n] ≅ M[p^n], and conversely; for maps of derived p-complete rings, bounded torsion ascends along p-completely flat and descends along p-completely faithfully flat maps, and then p-complete (faithful) flatness is (faithful) flatness mod every p^n.
items.note: DD.1: 'Prove the bounded-torsion criteria used for bounded prisms, complete flatness and complete faithful-flat descent.'

items.name: Avramov: Noetherian local complete intersections
items.statement: A Noetherian ring A is a local complete intersection iff L_{A/Z} has Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]; for Noetherian A → B of finite type, lci iff L_{B/A} has Tor amplitude in [−1, 0] (Quillen); hence p-complete Noetherian lci rings are quasisyntomic.
items.locator: Remark 4.11, Example 4.12 and Theorem 4.13, p. 224 ([Avr99, Thm. 1.2])
items.note: DD.0 plans the lci amplitude criterion 'in its finite-presentation/flatness range'; Avramov's theorem removes finiteness.

items.name: p-complete HKR theorem for quasismooth maps
items.statement: If A → B is quasismooth, then π_*HH(B/A; Z_p) is the p-completion of the exterior algebra Ω^*_{B/A}, the p-completed HKR graded pieces (∧^iL_{B/A}[i])^∧_p ≃ (Ω^i_{B/A})^∧_p[i] being concentrated in degree i.

items.name: Perfectoid rings
items.statement: A ring R is perfectoid if it is p-adically complete, some π ∈ R has π^p = pu with u a unit, Frobenius on R/p is surjective and ker(θ : A_inf(R) → R) is principal ([BMS18, Def. 3.5]).

items.name: A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and Fontaine's θ
items.statement: For a p-adically complete ring R, R^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R/p, A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) with its Frobenius automorphism φ, and Fontaine's surjection θ : A_inf(R) → R; θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{−1}. A_inf(R) is the universal p-adically complete pro-nilpotent thickening of R/p (used to identify π_0TP).
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165 at 082e2d3 defines fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R for R p-adically complete with p not a unit (surjective by fontaineTheta_surjective); PreTilt is Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634. The universal thickening property is planned in AI.0.

items.name: Basic properties of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For R perfectoid: ker θ is generated by a non-zero-divisor ξ = p + [π^♭]^p α; (L_{R/Z_p})^∧_p ≃ R[1], so L_{R/Z_p} has p-complete Tor amplitude in degree −1; R[p^∞] = R[p]; hence R is quasisyntomic.
items.note: The 'overkill' proof uses v-descent of Bhatt–Scholze (Witt Grassmannian); an elementary proof is also given.

items.name: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings
items.statement: S is quasiregular semiperfectoid if S ∈ QSyn, some perfectoid R maps to S, and S/p is semiperfect; equivalently S = R/I for a perfectoid R and a p-completely quasiregular ideal I (L_{S/R} of p-complete Tor amplitude in degree −1, for every perfectoid R → S). Z_p is not an example; perfectoid rings are. QRSPerfd is a site with quasisyntomic covers.

items.name: Quasiregular semiperfectoids form a basis: unfolding
items.statement: A p-complete ring is quasisyntomic iff it has a quasisyntomic cover by a quasiregular semiperfectoid (adjoin p-power roots of p and of generators; the cover is free mod p with free L[−1]); Čech nerves of such covers stay quasiregular semiperfectoid; restriction gives Shv_𝒞(QSyn^op) ≃ Shv_𝒞(QRSPerfd^op) for every presentable 𝒞 (F ↦ F^ℶ, the unfolding), compatibly with evaluation and graded pieces of filtered sheaves; the same holds for slice categories QSyn_A (A perfectoid or Z_p, where L_{B/A} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]) and qSyn_A.
items.locator: Lemmas 4.28, 4.30, Remark 4.29, Proposition 4.31, Remark 4.32, Variants 4.33, 4.35 and Lemma 4.34, pp. 229–231
items.note: DD.5 plans the 'existence/refinement of the semiperfectoid covers used by BMS2' and names 'the elementary compatible-root cover construction' as the BMS2 §4 argument. The proof of Lemma 4.34 has a misprint; see sourceIssues E2.

items.name: Proj-quasisyntomic O_C-algebras
items.statement: Over O_C (C perfectoid of characteristic 0), A → B of p-complete p-torsionfree rings is proj-quasisyntomic (resp. a cover) if B/p is a projective (and faithfully flat) A/p-module and L_{(B/p)/(A/p)} has projective amplitude in [−1, 0]; p-adic completions of smooth O_C-algebras qualify (finitely presented flat O_C/p-algebras are free), and the unfolding equivalence holds for qSyn^proj_{O_C}.

items.name: The filtered derived category
items.statement: DF(R) = Fun(Z^op, D(R)) with Day convolution (F ⊗ G)(i) = colim_{j+k≥i} F(j) ⊗ G(k); F(−∞) = colim F(i); F is complete if lim F(i) = 0; D̂F(R) is the complete objects, with completion F ↦ F/F(∞) left adjoint to the inclusion; gr^i are conservative on D̂F(R), commute with limits and colimits and satisfy gr^n(F ⊗ G) ≃ ⊕_{i+j=n} gr^iF ⊗ gr^jG ([GP18]).
items.note: DD.1: 'Construct filtered enhanced modules, … completed filtered tensor products, graded pieces, Hodge completion.'

items.name: The Beilinson t-structure on the filtered derived category
items.statement: For connective R, DF^{≤0}(R) = {F : gr^iF ∈ D^{≤i}(R)} and DF^{≥0}(R) = {F : F(i) ∈ D^{≥i}(R)} form a t-structure, compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure, with gr^i ∘ τ^{≤0}_B ≃ τ^{≤i} ∘ gr^i; for discrete R its heart is equivalent to the abelian category Ch(R) of chain complexes via F ↦ (H^•(gr^•F), boundary maps), symmetric monoidally. The t-structure is not left-complete; connective covers are Deligne's filtration décalée.
items.locator: Definition 5.3, Theorem 5.4 and Remark 5.5, pp. 234–235 (after [Bei87, App. A], [BBD82, 3.1.8])
items.note: The paragraph before Definition 5.3 has a misprint; see sourceIssues E1.

items.name: Ext groups in Ch(R) and an abelian-category recognition lemma
items.statement: For R-modules M, N, Ext^i_{Ch(R)}(M, N[c]) = 0 if c > 0 and Ext^{i−c}_R(M, N) if c ≤ 0; an exact functor G : 𝒜 → ℬ of abelian categories is an equivalence if finite filtrations by a class S and its image exist and G is bijective on Ext^* between objects of S.

items.name: Lη_I as a Beilinson connective cover
items.statement: For an ideal I ⊂ R defining a Cartier divisor and K ∈ D(R), Lη_I K is the complex underlying τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ K), the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration; consequently Lη_I preserves a triangle K → L → M exactly when the boundaries H^i(M ⊗^L R/I) → H^{i+1}(K ⊗^L R/I) vanish.

items.name: Lη_I is lax symmetric monoidal
items.statement: L η_I : D(R) → D(R) is naturally lax symmetric monoidal, hence carries E_∞-R-algebras to E_∞-R-algebras.
items.note: AI.1 plans 'its lax symmetric monoidal structure'; BMS2 derives it from item 041.

items.name: Derived de Rham complexes are quasisyntomic sheaves
items.statement: On QSyn_R the p-completed Hodge-completed derived de Rham complex (L̂Ω_{−/R}, L̂Ω^{≥•}) is a D̂F(R)-valued sheaf, and on qSyn_R (on QSyn_R if R is perfectoid or Z_p) the p-completed derived de Rham complex LΩ_{−/R} is a D(R)-valued sheaf, using the conjugate filtration mod p.

items.name: Hochschild homology of quasiregular semiperfectoids is even
items.statement: For S ∈ qrsPerfd_R (or QRSPerfd_R if R is perfectoid or Z_p), each ∧^iL_{S/R}[−i] is p-completely flat, π_odd HH(S/R; Z_p) = 0 and π_{2i}HH(S/R; Z_p) is the p-completion of ∧^iL_{S/R}[−i] ≅ Γ^i(π_1L_{S/R}), multiplicatively.

items.name: π_0 HC^- unfolds to Hodge-completed derived de Rham cohomology
items.statement: The sheaf (π_0HC^-(−/R; Z_p))^ℶ on qSyn_R, with the filtration from the homotopy fixed point spectral sequence, is canonically L̂Ω_{−/R}; on quasismooth algebras the heart description gives the de Rham complex (Ω^•_{A/R})^∧_p.

items.name: THH of perfectoid rings
items.statement: For R perfectoid, π_*THH(R; Z_p) = R[u] is polynomial on u ∈ π_2THH(R; Z_p) ≅ π_2HH(R; Z_p) = ker θ/(ker θ)^2, a generator; THH(R; Z_p) is pseudocoherent and THH(R; Z_p) ⊗^L_R R′ ≃ THH(R′; Z_p) for maps of perfectoid rings.
items.note: Reduces to Bökstedt's theorem by base change to the perfection of R/p and Nakayama; uses item 024.

items.name: TC^-, TP and THH^{tC_p} of perfectoid rings
items.statement: Generators can be chosen so that π_*TC^-(R; Z_p) = A_inf[u, v]/(uv − ξ), π_*TP(R; Z_p) = A_inf[σ^{±1}], π_*THH(R; Z_p)^{tC_p} = R[σ^{±1}] (via θ̃), with can : u ↦ ξσ, v ↦ σ^{−1}; φ : u ↦ σ, v ↦ φ(ξ)σ^{−1} (φ-linear); TC^- → THH : u ↦ u, v ↦ 0 (θ-linear); and THH → THH^{tC_p} : u ↦ σ. In particular π_0TC^-(R; Z_p) = π_0TP(R; Z_p) = A_inf(R) with φ the Witt vector Frobenius.

items.name: Reduction of TC^- and TP to THH and THH^{tC_p} over a perfectoid base
items.statement: For any connective E_∞-R-algebra A (R perfectoid), TC^-(A; Z_p)/v = TC^-(A; Z_p) ⊗_{TC^-(R;Z_p)} THH(R; Z_p) ≃ THH(A; Z_p) and TP(A; Z_p)/ξ̃ ≃ THH(A; Z_p)^{tC_p}; so φ : THH → THH^{tC_p} is recovered from φ^{hT} modulo v.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin twists over a perfectoid ring
items.statement: A_inf{1} = π_2TP(R; Z_p), free of rank 1 with φ-linear φ_{A_inf{1}} : A_inf{1}[1/ξ] ≅ A_inf{1}[1/ξ̃] inducing ξA_inf{1} ≅ A_inf{1}; A_inf{1} ⊗_θ R ≅ R and A_inf{1} ⊗_{θ̃} R ≅ ker θ/(ker θ)^2 = R{1}; with 𝒩^{≥i}A_inf = ξ^iA_inf: π_*THH(R; Z_p) = ⊕_{i≥0} 𝒩^iA_inf, π_*TC^-(R; Z_p) = ⊕_i 𝒩^{≥i}A_inf{i}, π_*TP(R; Z_p) = ⊕_i A_inf{i}, with can the inclusion and φ the twisted Frobenius.
items.note: AI.0 constructs A_inf{1} with 'source orientation'; this is the THH-theoretic definition.

items.name: Agreement with the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist of BMS1
items.statement: For p-torsion-free perfectoid R, A_inf{1} ⊗_{θ̃_r} W_r(R) ≅ ker θ̃_r/(ker θ̃_r)^2 with transition maps p times the natural ones, so A_inf{1} agrees with [BMS18, Example 4.24]: THH(R; Z_p)^{tC_{p^r}} = TP(R; Z_p)/ξ̃_r with π_* = ⊕ W_r(R){i}, using that TR^{r+1} → THH^{hC_{p^r}} is a connective cover and π_0TR^{r+1}(R; Z_p) = W_{r+1}(R).
items.note: The only place BMS2 uses classical TR (Tsalidis; Hesselholt–Madsen).

items.name: Tsalidis's theorem and π_0 TR
items.statement: If φ : THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} is a connective cover (e.g. A perfectoid), then TR^{r+1}(A; Z_p) = THH(A; Z_p)^{C_{p^r}} → THH(A; Z_p)^{hC_{p^r}} is a connective cover ([Tsa98], [NS18, Cor. II.4.9]); π_0TR^{r+1}(A; Z_p) ≅ W_{r+1}(A) with transition maps F ([HM97, Thm. 3.3]).
items.note: RT.2 proves 'agreement with the classical genuine-equivariant TR/TC formulation used by local K-theory calculations'.

items.name: THH is a one-parameter deformation of HH over a perfectoid base
items.statement: For an R-algebra A (R perfectoid) there is a T-equivariant cofibre sequence THH(A; Z_p)[2] →^u THH(A; Z_p) → HH(A/R; Z_p) of THH(A; Z_p)-modules, inducing TC^-(A; Z_p)[2] →^u TC^-(A; Z_p) → HC^-(A/R; Z_p) and TP(A; Z_p)[2] →^{ξσ} TP(A; Z_p) → HP(A/R; Z_p).

items.name: Antisymmetrization from differential forms to THH
items.statement: For any R-algebra A there is a natural graded A-algebra map μ_A : (Ω^*_{A/R})^∧_p → π_*THH(A; Z_p), from Ω^*_{A/Z} → π_*HH(A) (Connes differential), τ_{≤2}THH(A) ≃ τ_{≤2}HH(A), and the fact that Ω^i_{A/Z} → Ω^i_{A/R} has p-divisible kernel for R perfectoid.

items.name: Hesselholt: THH of quasismooth algebras over perfectoid rings
items.statement: μ_A linearizes to (Ω^*_{A/R})^∧_p ⊗_R π_*THH(R; Z_p) → π_*THH(A; Z_p), an isomorphism if A is quasismooth over R; and THH(−; Z_p) on p-complete R-algebras has a complete multiplicative filtration P^• with gr^n = ⊕_{0≤i≤n, i≡n (2)} (∧^iL_{−/R})^∧_p[n].

items.name: THH of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings
items.statement: For S ∈ QRSPerfd_R and M = π_1(L_{S/R})^∧_p: π_*THH(S; Z_p) is concentrated in even degrees; u : π_{2i−2} → π_{2i} is injective; π_∞ = π_0[u^{−1}] is an increasingly filtered R-algebra with gr_* ≅ (Γ^*_S M)^∧_p, so π_{2i}THH(S; Z_p) has a finite filtration with graded pieces (Γ^j_S M)^∧_p, 0 ≤ j ≤ i; each π_{2i}THH(S; Z_p) is p-completely flat over S.
items.note: The proof has a misprint (Γ^i_R for Γ^i_S); see sourceIssues E3.

items.name: TC^- and TP of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings; the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: For S ∈ QRSPerfd_R: the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences degenerate, π_*TC^-(S; Z_p) and π_*TP(S; Z_p) are even, and can is injective and an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 0; Δ̂_S := π_0TC^-(S; Z_p) ≅ π_0TP(S; Z_p) carries the complete Nygaard filtration with 𝒩^iΔ̂_S ≅ π_{2i}THH(S; Z_p), 𝒩^{≥i}Δ̂_S ≅ π_{2i}TC^-(S; Z_p) via v^i; φ maps 𝒩^{≥i} into ξ̃^iΔ̂_S, defining divided Frobenii φ_{S,i} with φ = ξ̃^iφ_{S,i}; Δ̂_S/ξ ≅ L̂Ω_{S/R} and Δ̂_S is ξ-torsion-free. Parts (1) and (2) do not depend on R.
items.note: Statement (2) has a misprint in the published text; see sourceIssues E4.

items.name: The motivic filtration on THH
items.statement: Each π_{2i}THH(−; Z_p) is a D(R)-valued sheaf on QRSPerfd_R, unfolding to QSyn_R with values in D^{≤i}(R); for A ∈ QSyn_R, THH(A; Z_p) has a functorial complete descending N-indexed T-equivariant filtration whose gr^i is an A-module with trivial T-action and a finite increasing filtration with graded pieces (∧^jL_{A/R})^∧_p[2i − j], 0 ≤ j ≤ i; it extends to all p-complete R-algebras by left Kan extension.

items.name: Nygaard graded pieces and the de Rham specialization
items.statement: For A ∈ QSyn_R, 𝒩^iΔ̂_A ≃ gr^iTHH(A; Z_p)[−2i] has a finite increasing filtration with graded pieces (∧^j_AL_{A/R})^∧_p[−j], 0 ≤ j ≤ i; Δ̂_A is (p, ξ)-complete with Δ̂_F = A_inf(F), 𝒩^{≥i} = (ker θ_F)^i for perfectoid F; and Δ̂_A/ξ ≃ L̂Ω_{A/R} as E_∞-R-algebras.

items.name: Nygaard complexes of smooth algebras over perfectoid rings
items.statement: If A is the p-adic completion of a smooth R-algebra of relative dimension d: 𝒩^iΔ̂_A ∈ D^{[0,max(i,d)]}, 𝒩^{≥i}Δ̂_A ∈ D^{[0,d]}, so (Δ̂_A, 𝒩^{≥•}) ∈ DF^{≤0}; H^0(Δ̂_A) has no φ^r(ξ)-torsion; and the linearized Frobenius factors as Δ̂_A → Lη_ξφ_*Δ̂_A ≃ φ_*Lη_{ξ̃}Δ̂_A of E_∞-algebras, with iterates Δ̂_A → Lη_{ξ_r}φ^r_*Δ̂_A.
items.note: PR.3 plans 'the Lη_I Frobenius factorization in BS22 §15'; BMS2 derives it from the Beilinson t-structure (item 041).

items.name: The non-Nygaard-completed variant Δ_A over a perfectoid base
items.statement: For A the p-adic completion of a smooth R-algebra, Δ̂_A/ξ ≃ LΩ_{A/R} (the Hodge and p-adic filtrations are commensurate); left Kan extension in (p, ξ)-complete A_inf-complexes gives A ↦ Δ_A on p-complete simplicial commutative R-algebras with Δ_(−)/ξ ≃ LΩ_{−/R}, a sheaf on QSyn_R with discrete values on QRSPerfd_R, a priori depending on R.

items.name: Motivic filtrations on TC^- and TP over a perfectoid base
items.statement: For A ∈ QSyn_R, TC^-(A; Z_p) and TP(A; Z_p) have functorial complete exhaustive multiplicative Z-indexed filtrations with gr^iTC^- = 𝒩^{≥i}Δ̂_A[2i] and gr^iTP = Δ̂_A[2i] and the resulting spectral sequences; on QRSPerfd_R they are the double-speed Postnikov filtrations.

items.name: Invertibility criterion for complete filtered modules
items.statement: For A ∈ CAlg(D̂F(Z)_{≥0}) and M, N ∈ Mod_A with η : M ⊗_A N → A: if gr^0M ⊗_{gr^0A} gr^*A ≃ gr^*M (and likewise for N) and η induces gr^0M ⊗ gr^0N ≃ gr^0A, then η is an equivalence and M, N are invertible.

items.name: Clausen–Mathew–Morrow: K-theory of rings henselian along p with semiperfect reduction
items.statement: If S is henselian along pS and S/pS is semiperfect (e.g. S ∈ QRSPerfd), the trace K(S; Z_p) → τ_{≥0}TC(S; Z_p) from connective K-theory is an equivalence.
items.note: Follows from Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's rigidity for henselian pairs (Theorem A there) and the semiperfect case.

items.name: The syntomic complexes Z_p(i)
items.statement: For quasisyntomic A, Z_p(i)(A) = gr^iTC(A; Z_p)[−2i] = hofib(φ − can : 𝒩^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i} → Δ̂_A{i}); for S ∈ QRSPerfd it is the two-term complex (τ_{[2i−1,2i]}TC(S; Z_p))[−2i] with H^0 = TC_{2i}(S; Z_p) and H^1 = TC_{2i−1}(S; Z_p).
items.note: The published definition prints gr^n for gr^i; see sourceIssues E5.

items.name: The syntomic complexes in weights ≤ 0
items.statement: Z_p(n) = 0 for n < 0, and Z_p(0) = lim_r Z/p^r as sheaves: π_iTC(A; Z_p) = 0 for i < −1, π_{−1}TC(A; Z_p) = coker(F − 1 on W(A)) is killed locally by Artin–Schreier covers, and locally S is w-local so K_0(S) is locally constant Z-valued functions.

items.name: Z_p(1) is the Tate module of G_m
items.statement: Z_p(1) on QRSPerfd is locally concentrated in degree 0 and equal to T_pG_m: for w-local S ∈ QRSPerfd with p-divisible units, K_2(S; Z_p) ≅ T_p(S^×) and K_1(S; Z_p) = 0, and such S (built by alternating w-localization and adjoining p-th roots of units) form a basis.
items.note: Uses item 063, K_1 = units and surjectivity of symbols onto K_2 for local rings, and Bhatt–Scholze w-localization. The proof has a misprint; see sourceIssues E6.

items.name: K_0, K_1 and K_2 of local rings
items.statement: For a local ring B, the symbol map B^× → K_1(B) is an isomorphism, B^× ⊗ B^× → K_2(B) is surjective and K_0(B) ≅ Z.

items.name: Syntomic complexes are locally discrete and p-torsion-free
items.statement: Z_p(i) on QRSPerfd is locally concentrated in degree 0 and p-torsion-free (Conjecture 7.18; equivalently the sheafified K_{2i−1}(−; Z_p) vanishes and φ_i − 1 is surjective). BMS2 proves the case i ≤ 1 and characteristic p, and shows p-torsion-freeness follows from a δ-structure on Δ̂_S; Bhatt–Scholze prove the conjecture.
items.note: Planned as a theorem: the Anschütz–Le Bras and AMMN extractions mark 'Bhatt–Scholze: the syntomic complexes are locally discrete' as planned in PR.4.

items.name: Z/p^r(i) commutes with filtered colimits
items.statement: The sheaf Z/p^r(i) = Z_p(i)/p^r commutes with filtered colimits in QSyn (two proofs: via item 063 and K-theory, and directly from the contracting divided Frobenius).

items.name: The divided Frobenius contracts high Nygaard levels mod p
items.statement: For C perfectoid of characteristic 0, A a p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebra and m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), φ_i and 1 preserve 𝒩^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p and φ_i − 1 is an equivalence on it (φ_i maps 𝒩^{≥m} into 𝒩^{≥m+1} mod p).

items.name: The Nygaard filtration on the de Rham–Witt complex
items.statement: For A smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p, 𝒩^{≥i}WΩ^•_A is the subcomplex p^{i−1}VW(A) → p^{i−2}VWΩ^1 → ⋯ → VWΩ^{i−1} → WΩ^i → WΩ^{i+1} → ⋯, a complete descending multiplicative filtration on which φ = p^•F is uniquely divisible by p^i (the largest such subcomplex), giving divided Frobenii φ_i = φ/p^i.
items.locator: Definition 8.1 and the following paragraph, pp. 265–266 (cf. [Nyg81], [IR83], [Kat87])

items.name: The Nygaard filtration recovers the conjugate and Hodge filtrations
items.statement: φ_i mod p : 𝒩^iWΩ^•_A → τ^{≤i}Ω^•_A is a quasi-isomorphism (φ_i lands in τ^{≤i}Ω^• and kills 𝒩^{≥i+1}); and WΩ/𝒩^{≥i} →^p WΩ/𝒩^{≥i+1} → Ω^{≤i}_{A/k} is a cofibre sequence.

items.name: Illusie: logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves
items.statement: For X smooth over k, W_rΩ^i_{X,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^i_X is the image of dlog[·] : G_m^{⊗i} → W_rΩ^i_X, and 0 → {W_nΩ^i_{X,log}}_n → {W_nΩ^i_X}_n →^{F−1} {W_nΩ^i_X}_n → 0 is exact as pro-sheaves on X_ét ([Ill79, Thm. I.5.7.2]).
items.note: The Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction routes the same Illusie sequence to CR.4 as a source.

items.name: Logarithmic forms as fixed points of the divided Frobenius
items.statement: For X smooth over k, 0 → WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] → 𝒩^{≥i}WΩ^•_X →^{φ_i−1} WΩ^•_X → 0 is an exact sequence of complexes of pro-étale sheaves, and WΩ^i_{X,log} = Rlim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}.
items.note: The proof has a misprint in the boundary case; see sourceIssues E7.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration and the décalage filtration of Lη_p
items.statement: Frobenius induces isomorphisms φ : WΩ^•_A ≅ η_pWΩ^•_A and φ : 𝒩^{≥i}WΩ^•_A ≅ Fil^iη_pWΩ^•_A = p^iWΩ^• ∩ η_pWΩ^•, so the Berthelot–Ogus quasi-isomorphism φ : Ru_*𝒪^crys ≃ Lη_pRu_*𝒪^crys is filtered (Nygaard to décalée).

items.name: The Nygaard filtration in the presence of a Frobenius lift
items.statement: If Ã is a p-completed smooth W(k)-lift of A with Frobenius lift, Illusie's comparison σ : Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)} → WΩ^•_A restricts to quasi-isomorphisms p^{max(i−•,0)}Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)} → 𝒩^{≥i}WΩ^•_A for all i ≥ 0.

items.name: Quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras
items.statement: An F_p-algebra S is semiperfect if Frobenius is surjective (S^♭ → S surjective), and quasiregular if moreover L_{S/F_p} ≃ L_{S/S^♭} is a flat S-module in homological degree 1 (S = S^♭/I with I quasiregular); these are exactly the quasiregular semiperfectoid rings of characteristic p.

items.name: A_crys(S) and its Nygaard filtration
items.statement: For S semiperfect, A_crys(S) is the p-completed divided power envelope of W(S^♭) → S (compatible with the divided powers on (p)), with Frobenius from S; 𝒩^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^iA_crys(S)}; Â_crys(S) is the Nygaard completion; A_crys(S)/p = D_{S^♭}(I).
items.note: CR.0 exports p-completed PD envelopes and A_cris; PR.3 constructs Nygaard pieces 'by the actual Frobenius-divisibility condition'.

items.name: The conjugate filtration on divided power envelopes in characteristic p
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra A and I ⊂ A, Fil_n^conj D_A(I) is generated by a_1^{[l_1]}⋯a_m^{[l_m]} with a_j ∈ I, Σl_j < (n + 1)p, equivalently by a_j^{[pk_j]} with Σk_j ≤ n; it is multiplicative and exhaustive, and there is a surjection Γ^*_{A/I}(I/I^2) ⊗_{A/I,φ} A/φ(I) → gr^conj_* D_A(I) sending a^{[k]} to ((pk)!/(p^k k!)) a^{[pk]}.

items.name: A_crys(S)/p is derived de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfect with I = ker(S^♭ → S), LΩ_{S/F_p} ≃ LΩ_{S/S^♭} is discrete and A_crys(S)/p ≅ LΩ_{S/F_p}, matching the conjugate filtrations (with Γ^*_S(I/I^2) ≅ gr^conj_*) and the divided power filtration with the Hodge filtration.
items.note: Extends [Bha12a, Thm. 3.27] (quotients of perfect rings by regular sequences, planned in DD.4) to all quasiregular semiperfect rings via S̃ = S^♭[X_i^{1/p^∞}]/(X_i).

items.name: The derived de Rham–Witt complex of quasiregular semiperfect rings
items.statement: Define LWΩ_(−) with its Nygaard filtration by left Kan extension from smooth F_p-algebras; there are fibre sequences 𝒩^{≥i+1}LWΩ → 𝒩^{≥i}LWΩ →^{φ_i mod p} Lτ^{≤i}Ω_{−/F_p} and LWΩ/𝒩^{≥i} →^p LWΩ/𝒩^{≥i+1} → LΩ^{≤i}_{−/F_p}. For S quasiregular semiperfect, LWΩ_S and each 𝒩^{≥i}LWΩ_S are discrete and Z_p-flat, φ_i mod p is injective, and LWΩ_S → S is a divided power thickening.

items.name: Structure of A_crys(S) for quasiregular semiperfect S
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfect: A_crys(S) is p-torsion-free; φ_i mod p : 𝒩^iA_crys(S) → A_crys(S)/p is injective with image Fil^conj_i; A_crys(S) ≅ LWΩ_S φ-equivariantly and compatibly with Nygaard filtrations; the image of 𝒩^{≥i} in A_crys(S)/p ≅ LΩ_{S/F_p} is the Hodge filtration, so Â_crys(S)/p ≅ L̂Ω_{S/F_p}; φ(x) = x^p on A_crys(S)/p. (The Nygaard completion differs from the divided power completion: for p = 2 the latter of Z_2 is F_2.)

items.name: A canonical complex computing crystalline cohomology of regular F_p-algebras
items.statement: For A a regular F_p-algebra with perfection S, R Γ_crys(A/Z_p) is computed by A_crys((S/A)^•) = A_crys(S) → A_crys(S ⊗_A S) → ⋯ (A → S is a quasisyntomic cover by Kunz and Popescu; A_crys(−) is a sheaf on QRSPerfd_{F_p} unfolding to crystalline cohomology). Whether there is a natural map, not a zig-zag, to WΩ^•_A is Drinfeld's Question 8.16.

items.name: TC^- of quasiregular semiperfect rings is Nygaard-completed A_crys
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfect the cyclotomic Frobenius and the one induced by Frobenius of S agree on Δ̂_S and reduce to x ↦ x^p mod p, and there is a functorial φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ̂_S ≅ Â_crys(S) ≅ L̂WΩ_S identifying Nygaard filtrations and lifting Δ̂_S/p ≅ L̂Ω_{S/F_p}.

items.name: TP of F_p[Q_p/Z_p] from HP of Z[Q_p/Z_p]
items.statement: With B = S[Q_p/Z_p], THH(F_p[Q_p/Z_p]) ≃ HH(Z[Q_p/Z_p]) ⊗_Z THH(F_p), and for connective T-equivariant M ∈ D(Z), M^{tT} → (M ⊗_Z THH(F_p))^{tT} is a p-completion; hence TP(F_p[Q_p/Z_p]) ≃ HP(Z[Q_p/Z_p]; Z_p) and π_0 ≅ L̂WΩ_{F_p[Q_p/Z_p]} (an argument of Akhil Mathew).

items.name: Segal conjecture in characteristic p
items.statement: For A smooth of dimension d over a perfect field k: gr^iTHH(A) ≃ (τ^{≤i}Ω_{A/k})[2i] and gr^iTHH(A)^{tC_p} ≃ Ω_{A/k}[2i], with φ the inclusion τ^{≤i}Ω → Ω; in particular φ : THH(A) → THH(A)^{tC_p} is an equivalence in degrees ≥ d (Hesselholt).

items.name: Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 on the Nygaard pieces of Â_crys
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfect and i > 0, φ_i − 1 : 𝒩^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S) is surjective; for all i ≥ 0 it is surjective as a map of sheaves on QRSPerfd_{F_p} (Artin–Schreier covers), using Fil^conj_{j−1} + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p.

items.name: Syntomic complexes of quasiregular semiperfect rings
items.statement: Conjecture 7.18 holds in characteristic p: for S ∈ QRSPerfd_{F_p}, Z_p(i)(S) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the p-torsion-free group A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}; there are exact sequences 0 → π_{2i}TC → π_{2i}TC^- →^{φ^{hT}−1} π_{2i}TP → 0 of sheaves on QRSPerfd_{F_p}.
items.locator: Proposition 8.20 and the preceding paragraph, p. 281

items.name: K-theory of quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfect, K_*(S; Z_p) vanishes in odd degrees and K_even(S; Z_p) ≅ ⊕_{i≥0} A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}; for S = O_{C_p}/p, after inverting p this is the graded ring defining the Fargues–Fontaine curve.
items.locator: Corollary 8.23 and the preceding paragraph, p. 283

items.name: μ, ξ, ξ_r and ξ̃ in A_inf(O_C)
items.statement: For C/Q_p perfectoid containing μ_{p^∞} and ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity: μ = [ε] − 1, φ^{−1}(μ) | μ, ξ_r = μ/φ^{−r}(μ), ξ = ξ_1 (generating ker θ), ξ̃ = φ(ξ), with ξ_r | ξ_{r+1} | μ.

items.name: Almost ideals in A_inf
items.statement: For d ≥ 1 and J_d = ∪_r (φ^{−r}(μ)^d) ⊂ W(𝔪^♭): p is a non-zero-divisor on A_inf/J_d and the p-adic completion of every J_d is W(𝔪^♭); so 'almost zero' may be tested with J_d.

items.name: Lη_μ as an almost limit of Lη_{ξ_r}
items.statement: For p-complete K ∈ D^{≥0}(A_inf) with H^0(K) torsion-free, every cohomology group of the cofibre of Lη_μK → Rlim_r Lη_{ξ_r}K is killed by W(𝔪^♭).

items.name: Almost elements of completed free A_inf-modules
items.statement: If M is the (p, ξ)-completion of a free A_inf-module, M → Hom_{A_inf}(W(𝔪^♭), M) is an isomorphism; RHom_{A_inf}(W(𝔪^♭), −) kills almost zero objects and is right adjoint to M ↦ M^a.
items.locator: Lemma 9.4 and the following paragraph, p. 285
items.note: The arXiv proof has a misprint corrected in the published version; see sourceIssues E8.

items.name: AΩ for all p-complete O_C-algebras
items.statement: Left Kan extension in (p, ξ)-complete A_inf-complexes of A ↦ AΩ_A = Lη_μRΓ(Spf(A)_C, 𝔸_inf) (for p-completed smooth O_C-algebras, with AΩ_A/ξ ≃ LΩ_{A/O_C}) gives a sheaf of E_∞-A_inf-algebras on QSyn_{O_C} with discrete values on QRSPerfd_{O_C}.

items.name: A Frobenius criterion for maps into AΩ
items.statement: In an ∞-category with endofunctor F, an object Y → F(Y) mapping to F(X) → X factors canonically through the limit of ⋯ → F(F(X)) → F(X) → X; applied to F = Lη_ξφ_* on E_∞-algebras in D̂(A^a_inf), the primitive comparison Δ̂_A → RΓ(Spf(A)_C, 𝔸_inf) (through all perfectoid A-algebras) refines to an almost map Δ̂^a_A → AΩ^a_A, using item 059.

items.name: Comparison maps on proj-quasisyntomic objects and the Cartier criterion
items.statement: For S ∈ qrsPerfd^proj_{O_C}, AΩ_S ≅ Hom(W(𝔪^♭), AΩ_S), so the almost comparison lifts to an honest map Δ_S → AΩ_S; and for A the p-adic completion of a smooth O_C-algebra, an endomorphism η of Ω_{A/O_C} (p-completed E_∞-O_C-algebra) whose mod p reduction is the identity on H^0 is an isomorphism (the Cartier isomorphism: H^* is generated by the Bockstein of H^0); Claim 9.7 checks H^0(d_A/(p, ξ)) = id on (A/p)^{(1)}.
items.note: The proof of Theorem 9.6 has a misprint (d_R for d_S); see sourceIssues E9.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration is the Lη_ξ filtration
items.statement: For A the p-adic completion of a smooth O_C-algebra, Δ̂_A → Lη_ξφ_*Δ̂_A is an isomorphism identifying 𝒩^{≥i}Δ̂_A with the filtration of Proposition 5.8; equivalently Δ̂_A ≃ AΩ_A carries the Nygaard filtration to the filtration from AΩ_A ≃ Lη_ξφ_*AΩ_A.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration in q-de Rham coordinates
items.statement: For a framed small A with deformation Ã and AΩ_A = q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf} (Koszul complex of ∂_q/∂_q log T_i), φ : T_i ↦ T_i^p realizes AΩ_A → φ_*η_{ξ̃}AΩ_A, and the Nygaard filtration is ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf} (as in Proposition 8.7).

items.name: Segal conjecture over O_C
items.statement: For A the p-adic completion of a smooth O_C-algebra of dimension d, gr^iTHH(A; Z_p) ≃ (τ^{≤i}Ω̃_A{i})[2i] and gr^iTHH(A; Z_p)^{tC_p} ≃ Ω̃_A{i}[2i] (Ω̃_A = AΩ_A ⊗_{θ̃} A), φ being the inclusion; so φ : THH(A; Z_p) → THH(A; Z_p)^{tC_p} is an equivalence in degrees ≥ d.

items.name: Adams operations act with weight i
items.statement: Z_p^× = Aut(T^∧_p) acts on THH(A; Z_p) = (A ⊗_{E_∞} T^∧_p)^∧_p and on all constructions; the action on Δ̂_(−) and its Nygaard filtration is trivial and on Δ̂_(−){1} is multiplication, so γ ∈ Z_p^× acts by γ^i on gr^i of THH, TC^-, TP and TC.
items.note: Rationally the filtration splits by Adams eigenspaces (Loday); BMS2 identifies the weights p-adically.

items.name: Quasisyntomic sheaves on formal étale sites
items.statement: A sheaf F on QSyn_{O_C} yields a sheaf on 𝔛_ét for a smooth formal O_C-scheme 𝔛 by F(𝔘) = lim F(R) over affine opens Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔘, since p-completely étale covers are quasisyntomic.

items.name: Syntomic complexes vanish above degree i mod p^n
items.statement: On 𝔛_ét the natural map τ^{≤i}hofib(τ^{≤i}𝒩^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n) → hofib(𝒩^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i})/p^n (maps φ_i − 1) is an equivalence: in coordinates φ(d_q log T_a) = ξ̃ d_q log T_a, φ − 1 is étale-locally surjective on Ã/p (Artin–Schreier) and ξ̃^{j−i}φ − 1 is invertible for j > i.
items.locator: Proposition 10.5 and the preceding computation, pp. 293–294

items.name: Fixed points of ξ^iφ^{−1} on A_inf,X
items.statement: For C = Rν_*𝔸_inf,X/p^n, 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} is a quasi-isomorphism on C/μ^jC for i ≥ j ≥ 0 (hypothesis (As)): injectivity by integral closedness of Ô_X^{♭+} ⊂ Ô_X^♭ and surjectivity by Artin–Schreier covers and tilting.
items.note: The printed computation has a misprint (μ^{i−j} for ξ^{i−j}); see sourceIssues E10.

items.name: Fixed points under (As) and under Lη_μ
items.statement: Assuming (As): 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1} is injective (ℓ = 0) or bijective (ℓ > 0) on H^i(C)/μ^j; 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} is surjective (ℓ = 0) or bijective (ℓ > 0) on H^i(C)[μ^j] and bijective on H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ]; and τ^{≤i}hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μC) → τ^{≤i}hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on C) is a quasi-isomorphism.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin prism and its embedding in A_inf
items.statement: 𝔖 = W(k)[[z]] with θ̃ : z ↦ ϖ, kernel E(z), Frobenius z ↦ z^p; K_∞ the completion of K(ϖ^{1/p^∞}); 𝔖 ⊂ A_inf(O_{K_∞}) ⊂ A_inf by Frobenius on W(k) and z ↦ [ϖ^♭]^p, faithfully flat and topologically free ([BMS18, Lemma 4.30]), compatible with θ = θ̃ ∘ φ and θ̃.
items.note: PR.0 lists the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) among its acceptance examples.

items.name: THH of the spherical polynomial ring
items.statement: THH(S[z]) = S[B^cy N] with B^cy N the submonoid (S^1 × N_{>0}) ∪ {0} of S^1 × Z, t·(s, n) = (t^n s, n); THH(S[z]) → S[z] is (s, n) ↦ n; φ_p factors through S[(B^cy N)^{hC_p}] via (s, n) ↦ (s^p, pn), so THH(S[z]) → THH(S[z])^{tC_p} lies over z ↦ z^p : S[z] → S[z]^{tC_p} (and S[z]^{tC_p} ≃ S[z]^∧_p by the Segal conjecture).

items.name: The cyclotomic structure on THH relative to S[z]
items.statement: For an E_∞-S[z]-algebra A, THH(A/S[z]) = THH(A) ⊗_{THH(S[z])} S[z] = A ⊗_{E_∞-S[z]} T carries a T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant Frobenius THH(A/S[z]) → THH(A/S[z])^{tC_p}, linear over z ↦ z^p, making it a cyclotomic E_∞-algebra over S[z].
items.note: The AMMN extraction routes 'Relative topological Hochschild homology over S[z]' to RefinedTraceMethods as a source.

items.name: Base change of relative THH: z ↦ 0 and z ↦ z^{1/p^∞}
items.statement: For an O_K-algebra A (z ↦ ϖ): THH(A/S[z]) ⊗_{S[z]} S ≃ THH(A ⊗_{O_K} k) compatibly with T and φ_p; after p-completion THH(S[z^{1/p^∞}]) ≃ S[z^{1/p^∞}], so THH(A/S[z]) ⊗_{S[z]} S[z^{1/p^∞}] ≃ THH(A ⊗_{O_K} O_{K_∞}; Z_p).
items.locator: Lemma 11.6, Proposition 11.7, Corollary 11.8 and Remark 11.9, pp. 301–302

items.name: Relative THH, TC^- and TP of O_K over S[z]
items.statement: π_*THH(O_K/S[z]; Z_p) = O_K[u], π_*TC^-(O_K/S[z]; Z_p) = 𝔖^{(−1)}[u, v]/(uv − E), π_*TP = 𝔖^{(−1)}[σ^{±1}] and π_*THH(O_K/S[z]; Z_p)^{tC_p} = O_K[ϖ^{1/p}][σ^{±1}], with can : u ↦ Eσ, v ↦ σ^{−1} and φ : u ↦ σ, v ↦ φ(E)σ^{−1}; 𝔖^{(−1)} is 𝔖 viewed as an 𝔖-algebra via φ.
items.locator: Proposition 11.10 and the preceding paragraph, p. 302

items.name: Relative theories of quasiregular semiperfectoid O_K-algebras are even
items.statement: For S ∈ QRSPerfd_{O_K}, THH(S/S[z]; Z_p), TC^-(S/S[z]; Z_p) and TP(S/S[z]; Z_p) are even and their homotopy groups are sheaves with vanishing higher cohomology on QRSPerfd_{O_K}; so gr^0TC^-(−/S[z]; Z_p) ≃ gr^0TP(−/S[z]; Z_p) is a sheaf of E_∞-𝔖^{(−1)}-algebras with Frobenius.

items.name: Frobenius-twisted Breuil–Kisin cohomology
items.statement: For Spf(A) affine smooth over O_K, Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} := gr^0TC^-(A/S[z]; Z_p) is (p, z)-complete with Frobenius, and (1) Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} ⊗̂ A_inf(O_{K_∞}) ≃ Δ̂_{A_{O_{K_∞}}} and ⊗̂ A_inf(O_C) ≃ AΩ_{A_{O_C}}; (2) ⊗_{θ^{(−1)}} O_K ≃ (Ω_{A/O_K})^∧; (3) ⊗ W(k) (identity on W(k), z ↦ 0) ≃ RΓ_crys(A_k/W(k)); (4) φ is an isomorphism after inverting φ(E). It carries a Nygaard filtration compatible with (1)–(3).

items.name: Frobenius descent of Breuil–Kisin cohomology by inverting u
items.statement: For an O_K-algebra A, φ extends to TC^-(A/S[z]; Z_p)[1/u] ⊗_{S[z]} S[z^{1/p}] → TP(A/S[z]; Z_p); for S quasiregular semiperfectoid the source is even and π_0 is a sheaf; and for A the p-completion of a smooth O_K-algebra, gr^0(TC^-(A/S[z]; Z_p)[1/u]) ⊗_{Z[z]} Z[z^{1/p}] → gr^0TP(A/S[z]; Z_p) is an equivalence (by item 086). Hence Δ̂_{A/𝔖} := gr^0(TC^-(A/S[z]; Z_p)[1/u]) satisfies Δ̂_{A/𝔖} ⊗_{𝔖,can} 𝔖^{(−1)} ≃ Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} and inherits the linearized Frobenius, proving Theorem 11.2.
items.locator: Proposition 11.15 and proof of Theorem 11.2, pp. 305–306
items.note: The published definition omits '/S[z]'; see sourceIssues E12.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration does not descend along φ
items.statement: The Nygaard filtration on φ^*Δ̂_{A/𝔖} ≃ Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} admits no functorial descent to Δ̂_{A/𝔖}: otherwise every smooth formal O_K-scheme would descend to W(k)[ϖ^p] (an elliptic curve with good reduction and j-invariant outside W(k)[ϖ^p] is a counterexample).

items.name: φ^*Δ̂_{A/𝔖} ≃ Lη_E Δ̂_{A/𝔖}
items.statement: The Frobenius φ_A : φ^*Δ̂_{A/𝔖} ≃ Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} → Δ̂_{A/𝔖} lifts to a filtered map 𝒩^{≥•}Δ̂_{A/𝔖^{(−1)}} → (E)^• ⊗ Δ̂_{A/𝔖} that is a Beilinson connective cover, so φ^*Δ̂_{A/𝔖} ≃ Lη_EΔ̂_{A/𝔖} (v^i = E^i/u^i; E is a non-zero-divisor on π_*TC^-(S/S[z]; Z_p)).

routes.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs
routes.brief: This route adds a source to the Part II of Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods proposed by the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction (RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs), which owns rigidity of K^inv for henselian pairs (their Theorem A). BMS2 uses one consequence, stated as Theorem 7.15: if S is henselian along pS and S/pS is semiperfect, then K(S; Z_p) → τ_{≥0}TC(S; Z_p) is an equivalence. Export it in this form: rigidity reduces to S/pS, and for semiperfect F_p-algebras the comparison is the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow computation. It is the bridge by which BMS2 identifies Z_p(0) = Z_p, Z_p(1) = T_pG_m and K_*(S; Z_p) = ⊕ A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i} for quasiregular semiperfect S (routed to RefinedTraceMethods RT.6). Unit tests: S = O_{C_p} and S = O_{C_p}/p, where K_2(S; Z_p) ≅ T_p(S^×) after w-localization and adjoining p-th roots of units.
routes.reason: The Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction proposes this Part II for rigidity of K^inv along henselian pairs; the comparison K ≃ τ_{≥0}TC for rings henselian along p with semiperfect reduction is its consequence, so it has the same owner.

RT.6 owns 'the BMS2 quasisyntomic THH/TC^-/TP computation and motivic-filtration interface' and the trace-to-prismatic comparison, so BMS2 §§5–7, §8.3 and §9 are its primary source (the planned items listed here). The missing items are the supporting constructions of those proofs: the non-Nygaard-completed Δ and AΩ, the almost-mathematics and Cartier steps of Theorem 9.6, the Segal-conjecture statements, the Adams operations, the invertibility lemma for Breuil–Kisin twists, the comparison with BMS1's twist, and relative THH over S[z] (which the AMMN extraction also routes to RefinedTraceMethods). They also include the K-theoretic identifications of Z_p(0), Z_p(1) and of K_* of quasiregular semiperfect rings, which the Bhatt–Mathew extraction routes to RT.6 ('syntomic complexes via algebraic K-theory').

RT.1 constructs Hochschild, cyclic, negative cyclic and periodic cyclic homology with derived tensor products, but plans only the smooth characteristic-zero HKR comparison; the integral HKR filtration obtained by left Kan extension, its p-complete quasismooth form and the universal property HH(A/R) = A ⊗_{E_∞-R} T belong there.

RT.2 constructs THH of E_1-algebras and its cyclotomic structure; the comparison THH(A) ⊗_{THH(Z)} Z ≃ HH(A) with the finiteness of π_*THH(Z) is the basic link between RT.1 and RT.2 that BMS2 uses throughout.

DD.0 plans the cotangent-complex lci amplitude criterion 'in its finite-presentation/flatness range' and the alternative formulations of quasisyntomicity in BMS2 §4; Avramov's theorem for arbitrary Noetherian rings, which BMS2 uses to put all p-complete Noetherian lci rings in QSyn, is the general form.

DD.1 constructs filtered enhanced modules, completed filtered tensor products and graded pieces; the Beilinson t-structure on DF(R) with its heart Ch(R), the supporting Ext computation, and the weak-Postnikov-tower lemma are the filtered homological algebra BMS2 builds on them.

DD.4 constructs the derived de Rham to crystalline comparison and 'the p-completed derived de Rham description of A_cris in Bhatt §9'; BMS2 §8.2 extends Bhatt's Theorem 3.27 to all quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras, adds the conjugate filtration on divided power envelopes, the derived de Rham–Witt complex and the structure theorem for A_crys(S), and gives a canonical Čech complex for crystalline cohomology of regular F_p-algebras.

DD.5 constructs the quasisyntomic site and its semiperfectoid covers 'used by BMS2'; the proj-quasisyntomic variant over O_C and the passage from quasisyntomic sheaves to formal étale sites are two further site-theoretic statements of the same kind.

AI.1 constructs Lη_f with its lax symmetric monoidal structure and Bockstein description; BMS2 Proposition 5.8 identifies Lη_I with the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration, which is how AI.1's filtered Lη enters PR.3 and CR.4.

AI.7 constructs Breuil–Kisin cohomology and must 'compare with BMS2 §11's trace construction'; the Frobenius-twisted complex Δ̂_{A/𝔖^(−1)}, the descent by inverting u, the non-descent of the Nygaard filtration, the Lη_E identity and the resulting constraint on de Rham torsion are that construction.

CR.4 constructs de Rham–Witt complexes with Frobenius, Verschiebung, dlog and the Lη_p fixed-point characterization, but does not name the Nygaard filtration; BMS2 §8.1 defines it on WΩ^•, relates it to the conjugate and Hodge filtrations, to the décalage filtration of Lη_p and to Frobenius lifts, and uses Illusie's logarithmic sequence (also routed to CR.4 by the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow extraction).
PR.3 constructs Nygaard pieces and 'the Lη_I Frobenius factorization in BS22 §15'; BMS2's explicit description of the Nygaard filtration in q-de Rham coordinates is a computation inside that layer.

PR.4 constructs the syntomic Tate twists and must 'prove the stated truncation and nearby-cycle/logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons under BS22/BMS2's hypotheses'; the lemmas of BMS2 §§7.4, 8.3 and 10 are those proofs (Theorems 1.15(1)–(2) are the planned items listed here).
